name: Cafés and coffee shops

problems.words: Pastries left at closing every day, we bin them
quick_ideas: Note ordered, sold and binned for each pastry for a week, so the next order isn't a guess
Order less early in the week than at the weekend, because demand isn't the same every day.

workzap_build.text: a tablet wastage log for pastries and milk that shows the trend by item and day and suggests tomorrow's order from what actually sold.

problems.ask_first: Are pastries baked in-house or bought in?
problems.free_stops: How order quantities are set by day and season is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which pastry trays still have pieces left at closing each day, so you see exactly where the binning keeps happening.
Give one person the daily pastry order decision and one notebook for leftovers, so ordering stops changing with each shift.

problems.words: I don't know my cost per cup, and bean prices went up
quick_ideas: Cost your best-selling drinks once from your latest bills, so you see which ones have slipped
Review prices on the thinnest drinks first, where the gap matters most.

workzap_build.text: a cost-per-cup sheet that updates when bean, milk and cup prices change and flags drinks below your target margin.

problems.ask_first: When did you last change menu prices?
problems.free_stops: The costing breakdown and repricing approach go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down beans, milk, cups and lids used on your busiest drinks once, so price rises stop hiding inside each cup.
Give one person the job of keeping supplier bills together in one folder, so cost checks stop waiting for spare time.

problems.words: Oat and almond milk run out on weekends, and milk bills keep rising
quick_ideas: Check milk, bean and cup stock on Thursday evening, so the weekend starts full
Note steamed milk thrown away each shift, because over-filled jugs quietly add up.

workzap_build.text: par levels for milks, beans, syrups and cups with WhatsApp reorder alerts sent to the owner when anything falls low.

problems.ask_first: Who checks stock and places orders now?
problems.free_stops: The par levels and reorder points per item are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which weekend shift runs out of oat or almond milk first, so you see where the refill plan breaks.
Give one person the Thursday stock check and one shelf note for weekend needs, so the rush starts with enough on hand.

problems.words: Coffee tastes different depending on which barista is on, and good baristas leave
quick_ideas: Put each drink's recipe in writing at the bar, so taste doesn't depend on who's on
Ask your best barista what would make them stay, because they rarely say it unless asked.

workzap_build.text: recipe cards with photos shared to every new barista, and a daily dial-in check recorded each morning across outlets.

problems.ask_first: How are recipes taught to new staff now?
problems.free_stops: The recipe standards and training flow stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Taste the same drink from different baristas on the same day, so you hear the difference customers are noticing.
Give one senior barista the handover job for drink standards each shift, so taste stays steadier when staff change.

problems.words: Morning queue is too long, and office coffee orders on WhatsApp get missed
quick_ideas: Split one person on orders and payment and one on the machine at the rush, so neither waits on the other
Ask office customers to order by a set time, so their runs don't collide with walk-ins.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp or web pre-order flow with ready-time slots, so office runs and regulars are queued in order and none are missed.

problems.ask_first: What time is your busiest rush?
problems.free_stops: The pre-order flow and slot set-up are described in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many office orders arrive during the morning rush and how many wait, so the clash with walk-ins is clear.
Give one person the job of writing every office order in one notebook, so chats stop disappearing during the rush.

problems.words: People sit for hours on one latte, and afternoons are empty
quick_ideas: Try one afternoon pairing offer in your quietest hours, to give people a reason to come and spend
Keep a few tables for short stays at peak, so seating turns when it matters.

workzap_build.text: sales by hour and top items every evening, so you see which offers actually lift the slow hours.

problems.free_stops: The offer plan by hour and how it's measured are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many afternoon tables stay occupied after only one drink, so the quiet hours problem has a real size.
Give one staff member the afternoon job of checking seated tables and clearing finished cups, so space looks active and ready.

problems.words: Card machine and POS totals never match, and staff give free drinks to friends
quick_ideas: Compare the POS report with the card settlement at closing, so a gap is caught the same night
Ring every free drink through the POS, so giveaways are visible.

workzap_build.text: a nightly close per outlet matching cash, card and POS, with free drinks and staff meals logged by shift.

problems.ask_first: Is the closing gap usually in cash or card?
problems.free_stops: The closing routine and free-drink rules are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each shift's free drinks beside card and till totals at closing, so giveaway patterns and mismatches can be compared.
Give one closing person the daily total check in one notebook, so card and till differences are caught on the day.

problems.words: No idea who our regulars are, and paper loyalty cards get faked
quick_ideas: Ask regulars if they'd like to join a loyalty list by phone number, with their permission, so stamps can't be faked
Notice and greet repeat faces, because recognition matters as much as the free drink.

workzap_build.text: phone-number loyalty at the counter for customers who opt in, with visit history recorded and abuse checks running in the background.

problems.ask_first: How do you reward regulars now?
problems.free_stops: The loyalty rules and reward design go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many familiar faces come in during one busy period, so regular trade is judged without relying on paper cards.
Give one person the job of marking repeat visitors by simple tally in one notebook, so regular custom stops being a guess.

problems.words: Instagram gets likes but I can't tell if it brings people in
quick_ideas: Ask new customers at the till how they heard of you, because it's the cheapest measure there is
Run one Instagram-only offer, so you can count who came from it.

workzap_build.text: codes and links showing which post or message brought which customer, counted as sales come in.

problems.free_stops: How codes are set up per post and tracked through to the till stays for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many customers mention your posts when paying this week, so likes are compared with people actually walking in.
Give one till person the job of tallying walk-ins who mention your posts, so everyone records it the same way.

problems.words: Second outlet's numbers I only see when I go there
quick_ideas: Ask the outlet lead for sales and wastage at closing, so you see it the same night
Visit at its busiest hour, not when it's quiet, to see it at its real pressure.

workzap_build.text: a short morning read with both outlets' sales by hour, average ticket and wastage, and the one thing to look at.

problems.ask_first: Do both outlets use the same POS?
problems.free_stops: What goes into the daily read and how it's pulled from each POS is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Have the second outlet note cups sold, pastries binned and cash shortfalls at closing, so your next visit starts with facts.
Give one person at the second outlet a fixed nightly send time for key numbers, so updates reach you without waiting for visits.

never_say: Anything about allergens, dairy alternatives for health reasons, or caffeine and health claims.
Food-safety or licensing advice, or how to handle a lease dispute — refer to the authority or a lawyer.
Help writing fake reviews or bulk-follow schemes.
That an offer or loyalty scheme will bring a set increase in sales.

sample_reply.person: honestly I need a fix for pastries. we throw out so many every night and I just guess the order each morning.
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there is a way through this, and the first steps are simple.
First, note how many of each pastry came in, sold and got binned for seven days, so the order stops being a guess.
Second, order less early in the week than at the weekend, because demand isn't the same every day.
Workzap could take this on by logging wastage on a tablet and showing the trend by item and day, so each morning's order is based on what actually sold.

Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
